title: Texas's 22nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Texas's 22nd Congressional District is an open-seat contest following the retirement of incumbent Republican Rep. Troy Nehls, who declined to seek re-election in 2026. The district, which covers portions of Fort Bend, Brazoria, and Harris counties south of Houston, is rated 'Solidly Republican' by the Cook Political Report. The general election pits Republican nominee Trever Nehls—Troy Nehls' identical twin brother and a retired Army colonel—against Democratic nominee Marquette Greene-Scott, an attorney, former teacher, and Mayor Pro Tem of Iowa Colony who previously challenged Troy Nehls in 2024. The race will determine whether the seat remains in GOP hands or flips amid a competitive open-seat environment.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the Texas 22nd Congressional District general election as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Trever Nehls
candidates.summary: Trever Nehls is the Republican nominee for Texas's 22nd Congressional District. He is a retired U.S. Army Colonel with 33 years of military service, including combat deployments to Iraq, Afghanistan, and Kuwait, and a 30-year veteran of Fort Bend County law enforcement who served two terms as the elected Fort Bend County Precinct 4 Constable. He is the identical twin brother of retiring incumbent Rep. Troy Nehls and has emphasized his conservative values, military and law enforcement background, and commitment to border security and supporting President Donald Trump's agenda.

candidates.name: Marquette Greene-Scott
candidates.summary: Marquette Greene-Scott is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 22nd Congressional District. She is an attorney, former high school and college mathematics teacher of 14 years, and currently serves as Mayor Pro Tem of Iowa Colony, Texas, holding Position 3 on the city council. A graduate of Southern University and the Paul M. Hebert Law Center at LSU, she previously challenged Rep. Troy Nehls in 2024 and lost 62% to 38%, but is running again on a platform focused on bipartisanship, infrastructure, economic growth, and community representation.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific general-election polling exists for TX-22 as of June 2026, so this forecast relies on district fundamentals and candidate context. The Cook Political Report rates this district 'Solidly Republican,' and the previous matchup (2024) resulted in a 62%-38% GOP victory—a 24-point margin. The open seat features Republican nominee Trever Nehls, the identical twin brother of retiring Rep. Troy Nehls, providing strong name recognition and continuity. Democratic nominee Marquette Greene-Scott is a credible candidate with local elected experience and has run this district before, but the Republican baseline remains overwhelming in this district. The absence of polling limits confidence to medium rather than high, but the available structural evidence points to a safe Republican hold.
